data_description.availability_entity: Optional Home Assistant entity whose state tells TaskMate whether this child is available. States 'on', 'home', 'available', 'present', or 'true' mean available; anything else (e.g. 'off', 'not_home', 'away') means unavailable. Leave blank to treat the child as always available. For calendars, wire up a template binary sensor since a calendar event usually means 'busy / unavailable'.
data_description.availability_inverted: When on, an active state (on/home/available) on the Availability Sensor means the child is unavailable. Use this for calendar or schedule sensors where an event means the child is busy.
data_description.unavailability_entity: A second sensor that indicates when the child is busy. An active state (on/home/available) on this sensor means unavailable. Useful for school calendars or schedule sensors. The child is only available when the Availability Sensor says available AND this sensor does not say busy.

data_description.claim_allowance_minutes: Extra minutes after this time-of-day window ends during which the chore can still be claimed. 0 disables the grace period. Night chores are always capped at midnight.
data_description.daily_limit: How many times per day this chore can be completed
data_description.schedule_mode: Choose how this chore is scheduled — specific days of the week, or a repeating interval. The scheduling options will be configured on the next page.
data_description.completion_sound: Sound to play when this chore is completed
data_description.visibility_entity: Home Assistant entity ID that controls when this chore appears. Leave blank to always show the chore. Examples: binary_sensor.dishwasher, sensor.soil_moisture, input_boolean.guest_mode, switch.laundry_room. The chore only appears on the child card when the visibility condition is met.
data_description.visibility_operator:
How to compare the entity's current state with your target value:
• No filter — always show the chore (ignores entity state)
• Equals — state exactly matches (e.g., 'on', 'home', 'running')
• Not Equal — state does not match
• Greater than or equal (≥) — for numeric values (e.g., 80 for battery ≥ 80%)
• Less than or equal (≤) — for numeric values (e.g., 30 for moisture ≤ 30%)
• Greater than (>) — for numeric values
• Less than (<) — for numeric values
data_description.visibility_state: The value to compare against. For 'Equals' or 'Not Equal': any text value (e.g., 'on', 'off', 'home', 'away'). For numeric operators (≥, ≤, >, <): enter a number (e.g., 25, 50.5, 100). Example: Entity 'sensor.temperature', Operator '>=', Value '20' shows chore when temperature is 20°C or higher.
data_description.assignment_mode: Everyone = every assigned child sees this chore. Alternating = one child at a time, rotating by day. Random = one randomly picked child per day (stable within the day). Balanced = today's balanced chores are split evenly across the assigned children. Unassigned = no child sees this chore — useful for parent-only tasks.
data_description.assignment_rotation_anchor: Day-0 of the alternating rotation. Leave blank to start today. Only used when Assignment Mode is 'Alternating'.
data_description.manual_start_child_id: Picks which child starts the rotation. For Alternating mode this permanently reorders the pool. For Random / Balanced it only overrides today's assignee — tomorrow's rotation resumes normally. Ignored for Everyone mode.
data_description.require_availability: When on, an unavailable child (based on the Availability Sensor in their profile) is skipped and the next available sibling takes the chore. Re-evaluated at midnight and whenever an availability sensor flips. Chores already completed today are not reassigned.
data_description.publish_calendar_entities: Pick one or more Home Assistant calendar entities. Whenever this chore is created, updated, or rolls over at midnight, today's assigned child is added as a calendar event on each selected calendar. Works with any number of calendars.

manage_task_groups.title: Manage Task Groups
manage_task_groups.description: Group chores so their assignments stay coordinated. Sticky forces all chores in the group onto the same child today. Spread gives each chore a different child.

add_task_group.title: Add Task Group
add_task_group.description: Only rotation-mode chores (alternating / random / balanced) can join a group, and each chore can belong to at most one group.

data_description.policy: Sticky — all chores in the group go to the same child today (the first chore in the list is the leader whose assignment the others follow). Spread — each chore is assigned to a different child today; if the group has more chores than children, it wraps.
data_description.chore_ids: Pick the chores to include. The order matters: for Sticky, the first chore is the leader whose assignee the others follow.

chore_schedule_recurring.title: Step 2 — Recurring Schedule
chore_schedule_recurring.description:
Set how often this chore can be completed. Once completed, it will not be available again until the window resets.

Note: Day of Week only applies to Weekly and Every 2 Weeks. Start Date only applies to Every 2 Days. Any values entered for inapplicable options will be ignored.

data_description.recurrence: How often the chore can be completed
data_description.recurrence_day: Weekly / Every 2 Weeks only — pin to a specific day. Ignored for all other recurrence types.
data_description.recurrence_start: Every 2 Days only — anchor date in YYYY-MM-DD format. Ignored for all other recurrence types. Leave empty to use today.
data_description.first_occurrence_mode: Available Immediately — child can complete it straight away. Wait for First Occurrence — chore is locked until the first scheduled day arrives.
